cases.query: A known classical reference experiment has more outcomes than input labels and may lose a linear direction. I can read the raw label once and want to choose both a release and its information budget after removing the external memory's own information. Is there a finite certificate?

My planar matrix energy has an exact rational angular primitive and a positive compatible-jet Gram identity. How can that premise give a lower energy gap for every full gradient variation rather than just rank-one tests?

Two conserving chains have identical individual control-clock laws, but one clock is shared. Can their rare circulation costs differ, and does the matching lower bound work after I reveal the whole initial configuration?

An experimentally sampled channel instruction is unbiased. I need a nonlinear recovery map involving an inverse square root; applying the map to each sampled instruction changes its mean. Is there a positive correction construction and what does it require?

A repair can let returning quantum memory choose an error on a damaged constituent. How can one common coherent outer decoder handle this without pretending every fault amplitude is a normalized channel?

Uniform nearest-neighbor quantum updates have selectable full resets with probability0.3. The simple two-child branching estimate fails. I want a finite-history local stationary sample and an unbiased gradient with paid variance.

A modular tensor scheme fails ordinary lifting and all infinitesimal deformations are exact symmetries. Would adjoining ramified coefficients rescue this same reduction, or is there a precise criterion to stop that search?

For a supplied finite centered Gaussian-mixture field I need the whole normalized finite-grid output without a height-gap premise. What exact route is available and which equally informed ordinary method should I compare it with?

I can sample a low-predictive-rank target and ask a different teacher for conditionals, with only a global KL mismatch promise. Which local error statement is valid and what prevents treating this as a completed robust sequential learner?
